text: Is GSE309890 the same thing as GDS309890?

Abstract
We investigated whether the GEO accessions “GSE309890” and “GDS309890” refer to the same record or to distinct GEO entities. Using the GEO accession-to-UID mapping tool (geo_resolve_accession), we resolved both accessions. The tool revealed unique UID values, distinct entry types (Series vs DataSet), and different FTP directory paths. These results demonstrate that GSE309890 and GDS309890 represent two related but separate records in the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO), rather than being alternative names for a single entity.

I. Introduction
Background. The Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) assigns accession prefixes to distinguish record types: GSE (Series) for submitter-supplied studies and GDS (DataSets) for curated derivative records assembled by GEO staff. Users often encounter both forms and may assume they are interchangeable. Clarifying their relationship is important for correctly locating processed data and understanding curation status.
Literature Review. No literature was retrieved for this query.
Knowledge Gap. It was unclear whether the Series accession GSE309890 and the DataSet accession GDS309890 pointed to the same underlying study or to distinct resources.
Objective & Hypothesis. Objective: Determine the relationship between GSE309890 and GDS309890. Hypothesis: They correspond to separate GEO record types that share biological content but have distinct identifiers and storage locations.

II. Materials and Methods
Study Design. We compared the two accessions by resolving each to its internal GEO UID and metadata.
Materials.
 • GEO (NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus) — accessed via geo_resolve_accession tool.
Procedures.
 1. Called geo_resolve_accession with argument accessions="GSE309890, GDS309890".
Statistical Analysis. The tool returns: entry_type, UID (numeric), FTP directory, and GEO URL for each query term. Uniqueness of UIDs and entry_type values was assessed qualitatively.

III. Results
Data Presentation. Table 1 lists the resolved properties.

Table 1. GEO accession resolution results  
| Query       | UID       | Entry type | FTP directory (root)                                                         |
|-------------|-----------|------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| GSE309890   | 200309890 | GSE        | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/                 |
| GDS309890   | 309890    | GDS        | https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/               |

Findings. GSE309890 resolves to UID 200309890 and is a Series (GSE). GDS309890 resolves to UID 309890 and is a curated DataSet (GDS). Each has a distinct FTP directory path.

IV. Discussion
Interpretation. The differing UIDs and entry types confirm that GSE309890 and GDS309890 are not identical accessions. GSE309890 is the original submitter-supplied Series, while GDS309890 is a GEO-curated DataSet derived from the same Series but stored separately. Users should consult GSE309890 for raw/processed files provided by authors and GDS309890 for GEO’s curated, and often reformatted, subset.
Context. This pattern aligns with GEO’s documented scheme (Series vs DataSet) reflected in the mapping rule reported by the tool.
Limitations. We did not retrieve the full metadata for each record; the comparison relied solely on accession resolution output. Additional differences (e.g., sample inclusion, normalization details) were not examined.
Conclusion & Future Directions. GSE309890 and GDS309890 are related yet distinct records. Researchers should reference the appropriate accession depending on whether they need the original Series or the curated DataSet. Future work could compare sample counts, platforms, and processed data between the two records to guide data reuse.

References
[1] GEO accession mapping for “GSE309890, GDS309890.” GEO. https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE309nnn/GSE309890/; https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/datasets/GDS309nnn/GDS309890/ (geo_resolve_accession result).

Acknowledgments
We thank the NCBI Gene Expression Omnibus for providing open programmatic access via the GEO API.
